# Fault inventory

<!-- generated by tools/faultscan.py --markdown; edit faults/inventory.toml -->

19 failure modes recorded while serving 500 GB-class DeepSeek MoE checkpoints
on consumer Blackwell. Each was reproduced here; `evidence` says what was
measured rather than inferred.

- **Measured on:** 8x RTX 5090 (sm_120, 32 GB per GPU), 2x Xeon Gold 6530, 503 GiB DDR5, PCIe Gen5 x16, no NVLink
- **Stack:** vLLM main @8c1d1c297, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, torch 2.13+cu130, driver 595.71.05, CUDA 13.2

## FI-001

### SM120 DSv4 sparse-MLA decode has no kernel for (topk=1152, page_block_size=32)

**blocker** · patch · `flashinfer` · affects DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on sm_120, sm_121

**Symptom.** The engine loads all 476 GiB of weights, offloads Engram and part of the expert
bank to host RAM, passes memory profiling, and then dies during CUDA-graph
capture -- roughly six minutes in -- inside the attention layer:

    ValueError: SM120 sparse-MLA has no decode kernel for this shape:
    num_tokens=8, num_heads=8, topk=1152, d_qk=512, page_block_size=32,
    model_type=1, extra_topk=0

**Root cause.** `csrc/sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4.cu` dispatches through a hand-written macro
list that enumerates 25 compile-time specialisations: `NUM_HEADS` in
{8,16,32,64,128} x `TOPK` in {128,192,256,512,1024}, with `PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE`
fixed at 64 by an early `if (mt != ModelType::DSV4 || page_block_size != 64)
return false;`.

V4.1-Flash asks for neither value.  Its sparse-index buffer is sized for the
widest layer -- 2 x `index_topk` (512) + the 128-token SWA window = 1152 -- and
the SWA cache it indexes has 32 tokens per page.  Both are outside the grid, so
no specialisation matches and there is no fallback.

Inside the kernel neither parameter is structural.  `TOPK` appears three times:
as the default and the clamp for `topk_len`, and as the row stride of the index
tensor.  `PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE` appears twice: as the divisor that splits a global
token index into (page, offset), and in the constant `pbs * IO_STRIDE` offset of
the scale footer.  Neither sizes shared memory, bounds a `#pragma unroll`, or
reaches a tensor-core tile shape.  FlashInfer already passes the *extra* cache's
page block size as a runtime `pbs_extra` and notes in a comment that "the
8-cycle runtime div is dwarfed by the cp.async.bulk that follows".

**Fix.** Make `TOPK` and `PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE` runtime arguments of
`sparse_mla_decode_dsv4_kernel`, leaving `NUM_HEADS` as the only template
parameter.  The instantiation grid shrinks from 25 kernels to 5 and every
`(topk, page_block_size)` becomes dispatchable.

    python upstream/flashinfer/apply_patch.py \
        "$(python -c 'import flashinfer,os;print(os.path.dirname(flashinfer.__file__))')"

The patch is reverted with `--revert`.  See FI-002: the prebuilt `.so` must be
moved aside or the edit has no effect.

**Evidence.** `tools/sm120_sparse_mla/probe_sm120.py` reproduces the failure from synthetic
tensors in seconds -- no checkpoint required -- and validates the patched kernel
against the PyTorch reference in `tools/sm120_sparse_mla/dsv4_ref.py`.  The
reference is itself validated on the four shapes FlashInfer already ships.

**Log signature.**

```
SM120 sparse-MLA has no decode kernel for this shape
decode-dsv4 launch failed \(unsupported shape or kernel error\)
```

See `upstream/flashinfer/apply_patch.py`, `upstream/flashinfer/ISSUE.md`.

## FI-003

### SM120 sparse-MLA prefill is a second dispatch grid, and V4.1 misses it on both axes

**blocker** · patch · `flashinfer` · affects DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on sm_120, sm_121

**Symptom.** With the FI-001 decode kernel available and the block size resolved, the engine
comes up, answers nothing, and dies on the first prompt long enough to prefill:

    tvm.error.InternalError: Check failed: (ok) is false:
    Unsupported sparse-MLA prefill configuration: model=DSV4 num_heads=8
    topk=1152 page_block_size=32 topk_extra=0 extra_page_block_size=0

**Root cause.** `sparse_mla_sm120_prefill.cu` is a separate dispatch from the decode one that
FI-001 patched, with its own compile-time grid. For DSV4 single-cache it
instantiates `TOPK` in {128, 192, 256, 512, 1024, 2048} and bakes
`PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE = 64` into every launch. For the dual-cache variant -- the one
compressed layers use -- it instantiates **only `topk == 128`**.

V4.1 asks for neither. `topk` is the SWA index row width, which vLLM sets to
`window_size + max_image_tokens` = 128 + 1024 = 1152 for the vision variant,
and `page_block_size` is the SWA cache's own block size, which vLLM hard-codes
to 32.

Inside the kernel `TOPK` is not a work bound. The tile count comes from the
*runtime* length: `actual_ni = ceil(topk_length / BI)` with `BI = 64`, and the
loops run `ti < actual_ni`. `TOPK` is only the index row stride, the clamp
ceiling, and the main/extra split point. So a wider row costs an allocation and
nothing else.

**Fix.** Two vLLM-side changes make the single-cache (pure sliding-window) layers
dispatch without a kernel rebuild (VL-011, VL-012): round the prefill index
width up to an instantiated `TOPK` (1152 -> 2048; 1152 is a whole number of
tiles, so the padding is never read) and ask the SWA cache for 64-token pages.

The dual-cache path -- every compressed layer -- is instantiated at
`topk == 128` only, so those two alone give text-only serving. The FlashInfer
edit in `upstream/flashinfer/apply_patch.py` adds the dual-cache
instantiations at `topk 2048` (FP8 compute mode, as the single-cache grid
already uses above 256, both extra page sizes): ten more kernels, no
arithmetic change. With it, `deploy/presets/v41-flash-vision.env` loads the
vision tower and serves images; every prefill index row is 2048 wide in that
mode, text requests included.

**Evidence.** Read out of `sparse_mla_sm120_prefill.cu` (`dispatch_dsv4_single`,
`dispatch_dsv4_dual`) and `prefill_kernel.cuh` (lines 95, 109-110, 130, 679,
693-698, 753). Reproduced on 8x RTX 5090: at width 1152 the error names
`topk=1152 page_block_size=32`; after padding, `topk=2048 page_block_size=64
topk_extra=512`, which is the dual-cache clause refusing anything but 128;
text-only, `topk=128` dispatches and the model answers correctly. With the
dual-cache instantiation at 2048 (kernels rebuilt, ~1 min): a 224x224 image
(231 prompt tokens) through `PRESET=v41-flash-vision` is answered "The image
shows a red circle."; the text probes on the same server stay correct, CUDA
graphs on.

**Log signature.**

```
Unsupported sparse-MLA prefill configuration
sparse_mla_sm120\.cu
```

See `upstream/flashinfer/ISSUE-prefill.md`.

## VL-009

### V4.1 on sm_120 has no working KV block size: its layers need two different ones at once

**blocker** · patch · `vllm` · affects DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on sm_100, sm_120

**Symptom.** Every value of `--block-size` fails, each somewhere different:

    --block-size 128 -> Assertion error (csrc/apis/attention.hpp:262):
                        block_kv == 32 or block_kv == 64
    --block-size  64 -> Assertion error (csrc/apis/attention.hpp:320):
                        ... (arch_major == 12 and ((is_fp4 and block_kv in {32,64})
                                                   or (not is_fp4 and block_kv == 64)))

and, before the backends are patched to offer 64 at all,

    ValueError: No common block size for 64.

**Root cause.** The DSA indexer's states-per-block is `block_size // tokens_per_state`, and
`tokens_per_state` is the layer's compression ratio. V4.1-Flash uses more than
one: its `config.json` carries

    compress_ratios = [0, 0,  2 x18 (layers 2-19),  1 x20 (layers 20-39),  0,0,0]

so the CED encoder half compresses two tokens per indexer state and the decoder
half one. A single `--block-size` therefore produces two different values:

    --block-size 128  ->  ratio-2 layers: 64    ratio-1 layers: 128
    --block-size  64  ->  ratio-2 layers: 32    ratio-1 layers: 64

DeepGEMM wants 64 from both. Its metadata entry point accepts 32 or 64; its
kernel entry point, on sm_120 with an FP8 indexer cache, accepts **only** 64.
So 128 breaks the decoder half and 64 breaks the encoder half, and no value
exists that works for both.

Compounding it, the DSv4.1 MLA and indexer backends both offered only `[128]`
off sm_90, so 64 could not even be negotiated until they were patched.

**Fix.** Fixed, and not by any of the three routes this entry first proposed. The
premise they shared -- that every layer must use one block size, so the
*kernel* block size has to differ from the manager's -- is wrong. vLLM already
lets each KV cache group carry its own block size, and this model already uses
four: the SWA cache asks for 32, the compressor for 8, the MLA/indexer group
takes `--block-size`.

What the DSA indexer kernel constrains is **states** per block, not tokens per
block. So scale each layer's block size by its own compression ratio and every
layer stores the same number of states:

    block_size = cache_config.block_size * compress_ratio   (ratio > 1)

With `--block-size 64`: ratio-2 layers get 128-token blocks holding 64 states,
ratio-1 layers get 64-token blocks holding 64 states. Both satisfy DeepGEMM.
Because their block sizes now differ, `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs.is_uniform_type`
returns False and they land in separate cache groups by themselves -- no change
to the allocator, and no change in bytes per token, since a ratio-1 layer
stores twice the states per token either way. It also generalises: upstream's
own V4 indexer backend declares `[256]` with the comment "C4 indexer pages hold
64 rows", which is exactly `64 x compress_ratio`.

Route 1 as written -- per-group *kernel* block sizes -- cannot work here.
`compute_layout_strides` asserts "Padded KV pages do not support kernel block
splitting", and V4.1's pages are always padded: 576-byte alignment against a
584-byte MLA state and a 132-byte indexer row.

`upstream/vllm/apply_patch.py` applies the scaling, plus a states-aware filter
in `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` so an illegal `--block-size` is refused at
startup with the constraint named, rather than aborting in a C++ assert during
graph capture six minutes in.

**Evidence.** Both block sizes were run to failure on 8x RTX 5090 with the FlashInfer FI-001
patch applied, and both DeepGEMM call sites were instrumented. At
`--block-size 64`: `indexer_spec block_size=64 num_states=32 tokens_per_state=2
kernel_block_size=64`, `mqa_logits kv_cache=(16, 32, 1, 132)
q_dtype=float8_e4m3fn q_scale=None` -- 32 rows per block, FP8, which the sm_120
clause rejects. At `--block-size 128` the ratio-2 spec reports
`num_states=64` and passes, and a ratio-1 spec then fails `:262` with 128. The
mixed `compress_ratios` come from the checkpoint's own `config.json`.

**Log signature.**

```
block_kv == 32 or block_kv == 64
No common block size for
arch_major == 12 and \(\(is_fp4
```

See `upstream/vllm/ISSUE-block-size.md`, `upstream/vllm/apply_patch.py`.

## VL-012

### The DeepSeek-V4 SWA cache asks for 32-token pages; every sm_120 sparse-MLA kernel wants 64

**blocker** · patch · `vllm` · affects DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on sm_120, sm_121

**Symptom.** Every sm_120 sparse-MLA entry point reports `page_block_size=32` and refuses
it: the decode dispatch as `no decode kernel for this shape` (FI-001), the
prefill dispatch as `Unsupported sparse-MLA prefill configuration` (FI-003).

**Root cause.** `DeepseekV4MLAAttention` constructs its sliding-window cache with a literal
`block_size=32`. FlashInfer's sm_120 sparse-MLA kernels are written for a
64-token page throughout: the prefill dispatch bakes `PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE = 64`
into every launch, and the decode dispatch had `if (page_block_size != 64)
return false;` before FI-001 made it a runtime argument. The two have simply
never agreed.

**Fix.** Ask for 64. The SWA backend already declares `MultipleOf(32)`, so it is a legal
request, and a 128-token window then spans two pages instead of four. Applied
by `upstream/vllm/apply_patch.py`. This alone would have removed half of FI-001
without any kernel change.

**Evidence.** `models/deepseek_v4_1/attention.py` passes `block_size=32`;
`sparse_mla_sm120_prefill.cu` passes `64` in all 30 of its DSV4 single-cache
launches (5 head counts x 6 topks).
Changed to 64 on 8x RTX 5090: the reported `page_block_size` becomes 64 and the
prefill dispatch's page-block axis stops rejecting the call.

**Log signature.**

```
page_block_size=32
SM120 sparse-MLA has no decode kernel for this shape
```

## FI-002

### Prebuilt flashinfer-jit-cache wheel silently shadows edits to csrc/

**major** · workaround · `flashinfer` · affects any on any

**Symptom.** Edit a kernel under `flashinfer/data/csrc/`, rerun, and the old behaviour
persists.  Clearing `~/.cache/flashinfer/<version>/<arch>/cached_ops/<module>`
does not help either, and no rebuild is logged.

**Root cause.** `JitSpec.build_and_load()` resolves to a `.so` shipped by the separate
`flashinfer-jit-cache` wheel, at

    site-packages/flashinfer_jit_cache/jit_cache/<module>/<module>.so

(906 modules on this install).  That path is consulted before the source tree,
so edits to `data/csrc` and `data/include` are never compiled.  The failure is
silent: the stale kernel runs and reports the old behaviour.

**Fix.** Move the module's directory out of `flashinfer_jit_cache/jit_cache/` before
testing a source change, then rerun -- the JIT path compiles from source:

    mv site-packages/flashinfer_jit_cache/jit_cache/sparse_mla_sm120 /tmp/

Restore it to go back to the shipped binary.

**Evidence.** Applying FI-001's patch changed the Python-side error to a C++-side
`ok == false`, proving the Python edit took effect while the CUDA edit did not.
Deleting the user JIT cache changed nothing; moving the wheel's directory aside
triggered a real nvcc build.

## FI-004

### SM120 sparse-MLA kernels gather row 0 of block 0 for every masked index and rely on 0 * row == 0

**major** · patch · `flashinfer` · affects DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Flash on sm_120, sm_121

**Symptom.** Any query whose sparse index row contains a `-1` (every partial 64-entry tile)
produces a non-finite attention output as soon as row 0 of block 0 of the KV
pool holds a NaN or Inf bit pattern. Queries whose rows fill whole tiles are
unaffected, which is how it presents: on a 132-token prompt tokens 63, 127 and
128..131 are finite and the other 126 are not.

**Root cause.** `io_bulk_gather_tile`, `io_gather_scales`, `prefill_kv_entry_base` and the
decode kernel's `issue_gather` all clamp a masked index with
`idx = (idx >= 0) ? idx : 0` and copy that row -- row 0 of block 0 -- into
shared memory like any other entry. The entry's score is then forced to -1e30
so its softmax weight is exactly zero, and the row is expected to fall out of
the P.V product. `0 * NaN` is `NaN`. The decode gather zeroes the scale word
for masked entries but still copies the FP8 payload and the unscaled bf16 RoPE
tail; the prefill gather zeroes nothing.

Block 0 is vLLM's null block: never handed to a request, and the designated
sink for padded and dummy work. It is not guaranteed finite, and under
DeepSeek-V4.1 it is not (VL-013).

**Fix.** Gather a row that is known to be finite instead of row 0: the tile's (or
chunk's) first entry. Index rows are compacted -- valid entries first -- so it
is a real row whenever the tile is iterated at all; the clamp to 0 stays as a
last resort. No arithmetic changes for valid entries. Five two-line edits,
carried by `upstream/flashinfer/apply_patch.py` as edit group FI-004.

**Evidence.** Read out of `kv_cache_io.cuh` (lines 82-83 and 108-109), `prefill_kernel.cuh`
(205, 212, 644, 916) and `decode_dsv4_kernel.cuh` (298-299). Reproduced on
8x RTX 5090 with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: block 0 of the layer-0 SWA cache holds
two NaN FP8 bytes in row 0 after CUDA-graph capture, and the raw attention
output of that layer is non-finite for exactly the partial-tile queries.

See `upstream/flashinfer/ISSUE-null-block.md`.

## PT-001

### Pinned host allocations round up to a power of two, and it is not configurable

**major** · workaround · `pytorch` · affects any host-offloaded model on any

**Symptom.** Host RAM runs out well before the arithmetic says it should.  For V4.1 the
Engram tables cost 264 GiB of the 503 GiB box instead of the checkpoint's
189 GiB, and the 75 GiB difference is what makes the configuration tight.

**Root cause.** The pinned-memory allocator rounds each allocation up to the next power of two.
Neither `roundup_power2_divisions` in `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` nor the same key
in `PYTORCH_HOST_ALLOC_CONF` changes it.

    requested   consumed
      8.00 GiB   8.00 GiB
      3.00 GiB   4.00 GiB
     11.80 GiB  16.00 GiB
      0.70 GiB   1.00 GiB

Engram is 16 shards (8 ranks x 2 tables) of 11.5 GiB each; every one rounds to
16.

**Fix.** Use plugin 0.2.0 with `DSV41_EXACT_PINNED=1` on the recorded V4.1 stack.
It registers page-rounded anonymous mappings for persistent weights, reducing
Engram storage to 188.83 GiB and also eliminating expert-buffer padding.
Activations and temporary async buffers keep PyTorch's allocator. For stock
allocation, sum the rounded size of every Engram and expert buffer; multiplying
only the requested offload budget by the rank count underestimates host RAM.
`tools/plan_memory.py --exact-pinned` models the new allocation path.

**Evidence.** Measured by requesting pinned buffers of known size and reading `Shmem` from
/proc/meminfo:

    requested   consumed
     8.00 GiB    8.00 GiB
     3.00 GiB    4.00 GiB
    11.80 GiB   16.00 GiB
     0.70 GiB    1.00 GiB

`roundup_power2_divisions` in `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` and in
`PYTORCH_HOST_ALLOC_CONF` both leave it unchanged.

It bites twice on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, and the second one is easy to miss:

- **Engram**: 16 weight shards round to 16 GiB each; 16 scale shards round
  to 0.5 GiB each, totaling 264 GiB. Small projection weights stay on GPU.
- **Expert offload**: a 12 GiB/rank budget spills 31 complete parameters,
  12.3926 GiB payload, occupying 23.5 GiB/rank. Scales are excluded from the
  budget. Thus 264 + 8 x 23.5 = 452 GiB, plus approximately 1 GiB of IPC,
  explains the observed 453 GiB of Shmem. The previous 29-buffer estimate
  incorrectly included scales in the offload budget.
- With exact allocations at the same budget, observed Shmem was 289 GiB.
  See benchmarks/results/2026-09-14-v41-optimization.md.

See `tools/plan_memory.py`.

## VL-001

### V4.1 startup validation checks a shape the model never requests

**major** · open · `vllm` · affects DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on sm_120

**Symptom.** An 8-GPU launch that cannot possibly serve a token spends ~6 minutes loading
476 GiB of weights before failing.  The guard that exists to catch exactly this
passes.

**Root cause.** `DeepseekV4FlashInferMLAAttentionSM120.__init__` calls

    has_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_config(self.padded_heads, required_topk)

with `required_topk = _required_sm120_sparse_topk(...)`, which returns the bare
`window_size` (128) whenever speculative decoding is off.  `(8, 128)` is in
FlashInfer's table, so the check passes -- but the runtime call carries the
*index-buffer* width, 1152, which is not.  The validated shape and the requested
shape are different quantities.

**Fix.** Validate the width of the index buffer that `forward_mqa`/`_forward_prefill`
will actually pass, not the window size.  That value is known at build time from
`index_topk`, `compress_ratio` and the SWA window.  Doing so turns a six-minute
load followed by a graph-capture crash into an immediate, actionable startup
error.

**Evidence.** Read from `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py` lines 83-91
and 585-592, and confirmed against the failing run: the guard passed and the
kernel then rejected topk=1152.

**Log signature.**

```
requires a FlashInfer DSV4 sparse MLA decode specialization for
```

See `upstream/vllm/ISSUE-startup-validation.md`.

## VL-002

### Pipeline parallelism is unusable for V4.1: input_ids are not forwarded across stages

**major** · open · `vllm` · affects DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on any

**Symptom.** TP4 x PP2 loads and profiles, then every stage-1 worker raises

    ValueError: DeepSeek V4 vision MoE routing requires input_ids.

Independent of `--language-model-only`.

**Root cause.** V4.1's MoE gate keeps separate expert-selection biases for text and image
tokens, so the routing function needs `input_ids`.  vLLM's pipeline boundary
carries hidden states and residuals, not token ids, so stage 1 has no way to
recover them.

**Fix.** Either propagate `input_ids` in the pipeline IntermediateTensors for models that
declare they need it, or precompute the per-token text/image routing mask on
stage 0 and carry that instead -- it is one bool per token rather than a vocab
index, and it is what the gate actually consumes.

**Evidence.** Reproduced on TP4 x PP2 at two offload settings (`/data/runs/boot-attempt3`,
`/data/runs/boot-attempt4`).  Rules out pipeline parallelism as a way to trade
the 8 GPUs' memory against the expert bank.

**Log signature.**

```
DeepSeek V4 vision MoE routing requires input_ids
```

See `upstream/vllm/ISSUE-pp-input-ids.md`.

## VL-003

### FlashInfer autotuning inside a collective barrier hangs multi-GPU startup

**major** · workaround · `vllm` · affects any MoE on sm_120 on sm_120

**Symptom.** An 8-GPU launch dies about 40 minutes in with a gloo `Connection closed by
peer`, after minutes of no output.

**Root cause.** `kernel_warmup` calls `flashinfer_autotune`, which JIT-compiles sm_120 kernels
while the ranks sit in a collective.  Compilation times differ per rank by
minutes; a peer exceeds the gloo timeout and drops, taking the run with it.

**Fix.** --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}'

Startup then takes about 3 minutes instead of failing after 40.  A real fix
would compile outside the collective, or barrier with a timeout scaled to the
compile.

**Evidence.** Measured: 40 min to failure with autotune on, 3 min to ready with it off.

**Log signature.**

```
Connection closed by peer
(?<!enable_)flashinfer_autotune
```

## VL-004

### Strict NUMA binding can OOM-kill a host-heavy MoE

**major** · workaround · `vllm` · affects any host-offloaded MoE on multi-socket

**Symptom.** With Engram plus offloaded experts, one worker is killed by the kernel:

    oom-kill:constraint=CONSTRAINT_MEMORY_POLICY,nodemask=0

**Root cause.** The four workers bound to one socket together need more than that socket's
251 GiB, and a bound process cannot spill to the other node.

**Fix.** Leave strict `--numa-bind` off for the original rounded-allocation preset.
Check per-node capacity and page placement before enabling it elsewhere.
Single-GPU UVA bandwidth (51.3 local / 51.1 remote GB/s) did not expose
contention: eight concurrent readers measured 260.3 local / 197.4 remote GB/s
aggregate. The exact-pinned serving workers already allocate nearly all host
weights on their GPU's local node without this flag.

**Evidence.** UVA micro-benchmark on GPU6/membind1 and GPU7/membind0 (`scripts/bench/uva_bench.py`),
and the V4-Flash matrix rows `TP8 + EP` vs `TP8 + EP + --numa-bind`.

**Log signature.**

```
oom-kill:constraint=CONSTRAINT_MEMORY_POLICY
```

See `scripts/bench/uva_bench.py`, `scripts/bench/numa_bandwidth.py`.

## VL-010

### nvcc off PATH disables every FlashInfer backend, and is reported as a missing kernel build

**major** · workaround · `vllm` · affects any on any

**Symptom.** A launch that worked interactively fails from systemd, cron, or a script:

    RuntimeError: FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4 on SM120 requires a FlashInfer
    DSV4 sparse MLA decode specialization for (num_q_heads=8, top_k=128).
    Install a FlashInfer build containing flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4380.

The named specialisation is present.  Rebuilding FlashInfer changes nothing.

**Root cause.** `has_flashinfer()` is `find_spec("flashinfer") and (has_flashinfer_cubin() or
shutil.which("nvcc"))`.  Without the `flashinfer-cubin` package, every
FlashInfer capability query returns False whenever `nvcc` is not on `PATH` --
which is the normal state of a non-interactive shell on a box where CUDA lives
in `/usr/local/cuda`.  The model-level guard then reports the *consequence*
(no specialisation) rather than the *cause* (no compiler), and points at a
FlashInfer PR.

**Fix.** export PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin:$PATH

`deploy/serve.sh` does this automatically and `deploy/preflight.py` checks it.
Upstream, the two conditions deserve distinct messages: "FlashInfer is
unavailable in this environment (nvcc not found, flashinfer-cubin not
installed)" is a ten-second fix; "FlashInfer lacks this kernel" is an afternoon.

**Evidence.** Reproduced by launching the identical command from a non-login shell; adding
`/usr/local/cuda/bin` to PATH made it start.  Confirmed by calling
`vllm.utils.flashinfer.has_flashinfer()` directly, which returned False while
`from flashinfer.decode import trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` succeeded.

**Log signature.**

```
Install a FlashInfer build containing
```

See `deploy/preflight.py`.

## VL-011

### Text-only serving still widens the SWA prefill index for images that cannot arrive

**major** · patch · `vllm` · affects DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Flash on all

**Symptom.** `--language-model-only` and `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0}'` both log
"running in text-only mode", and the SWA prefill index rows are still sized
`window_size + max_image_tokens`. On sm_120 that is the difference between a
model that serves and one that cannot dispatch a prefill kernel (FI-003);
everywhere else it is wasted index-building work and memory on every prefill.

**Root cause.** `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadataBuilder` keys the widening off the *architecture*:

    self.max_image_tokens = (
        getattr(hf_config, "vision_max_n_token", 0)
        if getattr(hf_config, "vision_n_layers", 0) > 0
        else 0
    )

`vision_n_layers > 0` says the checkpoint has a vision tower. It does not say
this engine will ever be handed an image. Text-only mode is expressed in the
multimodal config -- `get_limit_per_prompt("image") == 0`, which
`language_model_only` also forces -- and the hf_config attribute is untouched
by either.

**Fix.** Gate the widening on whether images can actually arrive, not on whether the
checkpoint could accept them. `upstream/vllm/apply_patch.py` adds
`images_can_arrive(vllm_config)` and uses it in both the SWA metadata builder
and the V4.1 attention layer's JIT warmup key, so the warmup key matches the
shape the kernel is actually called with.

**Evidence.** Measured on 8x RTX 5090: with `--language-model-only`, `ModelConfig.hf_config`
still reports `vision_n_layers=32 vision_max_n_token=1024` while the registry
logs "All limits of multimodal modalities supported by the model are set to 0,
running in text-only mode". Prefill index width stays 1152 until the gate is
added, then becomes 128 and the dual-cache prefill kernel dispatches.

**Log signature.**

```
Unsupported sparse-MLA prefill configuration: model=DSV4 num_heads=\d+ topk=1152
```

See `upstream/vllm/ISSUE-prefill-width.md`.

## VL-013

### CUDA-graph capture writes V4.1 state into the null block, which the sm_120 sparse-MLA kernels gather for every masked index

**major** · patch · `vllm` · affects DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on sm_120

**Symptom.** With CUDA graphs enabled the server comes up, captures cleanly, and answers
every request with non-finite logits: the same token id forever, an empty
completion, `logprobs` rejected as "Out of range float values are not JSON
compliant", and an illegal memory access on longer prompts. The first request
of a fresh server is already wrong, and it is an eager prefill above every
captured size, so no graph is replayed for it.

With `--enforce-eager` the same build answers correctly.

**Root cause.** Two halves, one in vLLM and one in FlashInfer, and both have to hold for the
model to break.

**vLLM writes into block 0.** `capture_model` warms each graph up with dummy
forwards whose block tables are all zeros and whose slot mapping is
`PAD_SLOT_ID`. The plain KV inserts honour the pad and write nothing. Three
V4.1 writers never look at it: the compressed-KV and indexer-K slots come from
`get_compressed_slot_mapping(...)` over the block table, and the fp32
compressor state ring's slot is `block_table[req, 0]`. All three resolve to
block 0 -- the null block, which the scheduler never hands to a request and
which starts as `torch.zeros`. Hybrid KV groups overlay one buffer, so the fp32
state ring lands on top of layer 0's sliding-window cache. Read back after
capture: 8143 non-zero bytes in rows 0..7 of that block, two NaN bytes in the
FP8 payload of row 0. In eager mode the block is all zeros.

**FlashInfer reads block 0 for every `-1`.** `io_bulk_gather_tile`,
`io_gather_scales`, `prefill_kv_entry_base` and the decode kernel's gather all
do `idx = (idx >= 0) ? idx : 0`: a masked index is clamped to row 0 of block 0
and its row is copied into shared memory. The entry's score is forced to
-1e30, so its softmax weight is exactly zero -- and `0 * NaN` is `NaN`. Every
query whose index row ends in a partial 64-entry tile carries at least one
`-1`; every one of them comes back NaN. On a 132-token prompt the finite
tokens are exactly 63, 127 and 128..131, the ones whose sliding window fills
whole tiles.

Bisected on the real checkpoint, one boot per row: eager correct; graphs with
the memory-profiling capture skipped, corrupt; graphs with `capture_model`
skipped, correct; graphs with only capture's dummy warm-up forwards and no
graph recorded, corrupt; graphs with block 0 zeroed after capture, correct.
The graphs are innocent. The forwards run to warm them up are not.

Neither half exists in DeepSeek-V4 in this shape, which is why V4-Flash is
correct with graphs on the same build.

**Fix.** Both sides are patched here and either alone is enough:

- `upstream/vllm/apply_patch.py` zeroes block 0 of every KV cache view at the
  end of `capture_model` (the null block is never allocated to a request, so
  this is exact and free).
- `upstream/flashinfer/apply_patch.py` (edit group FI-004) makes the kernels
  gather the tile's first entry for a masked index instead of row 0; index
  rows are compacted, so that is a real, finite row whenever the tile is
  iterated at all.

`--enforce-eager` is no longer required. `deploy/presets/v41-flash.env` runs
with CUDA graphs on.

**Evidence.** 8x RTX 5090, vLLM main @8c1d1c297, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1. Per-layer
finiteness hooks (a throwaway vLLM plugin) on the first post-capture forward:
embeddings, q, kv, layer-0 weights and RoPE cache finite; raw sparse-MLA
output non-finite for 126/132 tokens, finite for 63, 127, 128..131. Dump of
layer-0 SWA block 0 after capture: 8143 non-zero bytes, row 0 with 2 NaN FP8
bytes; the eager control's block 0 is all zeros. With block 0 zeroed after
capture: graphs on, 6/6 continuations, "$8" on the word problem, 94 graph
replays with finite logits. Raw runs in `benchmarks/results/2026-09-14-v41-cudagraphs.md`.

**Log signature.**

```
an illegal memory access was encountered
Out of range float values are not JSON compliant
```

See `upstream/vllm/ISSUE-v41-cudagraphs.md`, `upstream/flashinfer/ISSUE-null-block.md`.

## VL-014

### Adaptive DSpark verification is unsupported by the SM120 indexer backend

**major** · workaround · `vllm` · affects DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with adaptive DSpark verification on sm_120

**Symptom.** Startup fails after loading weights:

    Adaptive verification trims verification requests on device, which the
    DeepseekV41IndexerBackend attention backend does not support.

**Root cause.** Adaptive verification requires device-decided query lengths. The recorded
SM120 indexer backend does not support that contract. Correct CUDA graph
capture alone does not make the adaptive path available.

**Fix.** Use static verification: set `enable_adaptive_verification=false` in the
speculative configuration, as in `v41-flash-latency`. Do not bypass the backend
support gate. Supporting adaptive verification requires an indexer kernel and
metadata path that honor device-side lengths, then graph and output validation.

**Evidence.** Adaptive DSpark-5 failed at startup on the reference eight-GPU host. Static
DSpark-5 passed sanity checks, repeated serving workloads, and 32K/8x8K cache
probes. See benchmarks/results/2026-09-14-v41-optimization.md.

**Log signature.**

```
Adaptive verification trims verification requests on device
```

See `deploy/presets/v41-flash-latency.env`, `benchmarks/results/2026-09-14-v41-optimization.md`.

## VL-005

### --block-size is model-specific and silently non-portable

**minor** · open · `vllm` · affects DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Flash on any

**Symptom.** A launcher that works for V4.1 fails on the V4-Flash NVFP4 checkpoint with

    No common block size for 128

**Root cause.** `DeepseekV4FlashInferMLASparseBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()`
returns `[128]`, so V4.1 requires `--block-size 128`.  The V4-Flash NVFP4
backend does not accept it.  The flag reads like a tuning knob and is really a
backend constraint.

**Fix.** Leave `--block-size` unset and let vLLM negotiate it, unless a backend demands
otherwise.  Keep per-model launchers rather than one parameterised script.

**Evidence.** Both failures reproduced while porting the V4.1 launcher to V4-Flash.

**Log signature.**

```
No common block size for
```

## VL-008

### UVAOffloader materialises two host copies per tensor

**minor** · patch · `vllm` · affects any host-offloaded model on any

**Symptom.** Host-memory peak during weight load is higher and less predictable than the
steady-state pinned total.

**Root cause.** The stock offloader makes a pageable host copy of each tensor and then a pinned
copy, so two buffers exist at once.

**Fix.** `vllm_dsv41_opt` allocates the pinned buffer once.  Install it with
`pip install ./vllm_dsv41_opt`.

Do not expect it to rescue a configuration.  A controlled A/B on V4-Flash at
6 GiB/rank showed no measurable difference in peak `Shmem` (48.4 GiB both ways)
or throughput (56.0 vs 56.1 tok/s): the transient it removes is anonymous
memory, not pinned.  It is kept because it makes the peak deterministic.

**Evidence.** V4-Flash matrix rows `6 GiB/rank` vs `6 GiB, stock two-copy offload`.

See `vllm_dsv41_opt/`.

## VL-006

### MXFP4 MoE pads the per-rank intermediate size, inflating expert bytes by up to 1.33x

**perf** · workaround · `vllm` · affects any MXFP4 MoE on sm_120

**Symptom.** Expert weights occupy noticeably more GPU memory than the checkpoint implies,
and the excess grows as tensor parallelism grows.

**Root cause.** The MXFP4 MoE backends pad the per-rank intermediate size to their tile width.
For V4.1 (`moe_intermediate_size` 2304, 40 layers):

    layout                          intermediate/rank  padded   bytes/rank
    TP8, Marlin / DeepGEMM / TRTLLM        288          384      44.8 GiB
    TP8, Triton                            288          320      37.4 GiB
    TP4, Marlin                            576          640      74.7 GiB
    EP8, whole experts                    2304         2304      33.6 GiB

**Fix.** Use `--enable-expert-parallel`.  Whole experts are never split, so nothing is
padded, and it is the largest single win measured on this box: +79 % single
stream, +94 % at 8 streams, +28 % at 32, with prefill unchanged and startup a
third shorter.

**Evidence.** V4-Flash 8-GPU matrix, rows `TP8 baseline` vs `TP8 + expert parallel`.

See `benchmarks/results/2026-09-13-overnight.md`.

## VL-007

### Host offload costs decode throughput roughly linearly in offloaded bytes

**perf** · open · `vllm` · affects any host-offloaded MoE on PCIe-only

**Symptom.** Every offloaded gigabyte is paid back on every decode step.  On V4-Flash with
expert parallelism: 6 GiB/rank costs half the decode throughput and two thirds
of prefill; 12 GiB/rank costs about 70 % and 80 %.

**Root cause.** Offloaded expert weights are read over PCIe on each step.  Zero-copy UVA reads
reach 51.3 GB/s -- 91 % of plain host-to-device bandwidth -- so the transfer is
already near the hardware limit; the cost is structural, not an implementation
defect.

**Fix.** Offload the minimum that makes the model fit, and spend effort on shrinking the
resident bytes instead (expert parallelism first, then expert quantisation).
`tools/plan_memory.py --tp 8 --ep` reports the smallest offload that fits.

**Evidence.** V4-Flash matrix at 0 / 6 / 12 GiB per rank, plus GPT-OSS-120B at 0 / 4 / 10.1 /
14.1 GiB per rank, which isolates the effect on the same MXFP4 kernels.

See `benchmarks/results/2026-09-13-overnight.md`.
